claims.text: High-entropy alloys containing a balanced mixture of magnetic elements such as Mn, Fe, and Ni can be engineered to exhibit improved magnetocaloric effects.
Compositional disorder enables the magnetic phase transitions of these HEAs to be tuned.
The proposed initial material is a disordered solid-solution HEA with either an FCC or BCC structure.
The proposed HEA has near-equiatomic contents of transition metals such as Mn, Fe, and Ni.
Adjusting alloy composition can maximize the magnetic contributions of the constituent elements.
Adjusting alloy composition can induce an optimized, reversible magnetic phase transition near the operational temperature.
A disordered solid-solution structure produces a complex local magnetic environment with diverse atomic interactions.
The configurational entropy of HEAs creates a broad range of local magnetic interactions.
A broad range of local magnetic interactions can produce a more gradual and tunable magnetic phase transition.
A more gradual and tunable magnetic phase transition enhances the magnetic entropy change generated by an applied magnetic field.
Magnetic entropy change is a key parameter of magnetocaloric performance.
An optimized HEA is expected to exhibit a larger field-induced magnetic entropy change than conventional magnetocaloric alloys.
The larger magnetic entropy change is expected to result in higher magnetocaloric efficiency.
Any improvement is expected only within a specific composition and temperature window in which the HEA has a reversible magnetic phase transition.
There is limited direct evidence connecting HEA compositions with enhanced magnetocaloric effects.
